   City Council Staff Report

  DATE: March 1, 2023
  AGENDA ITEM NO:  1

 TO:  The Honorable Mayor and City Council

 FROM:  Ron Bow, City Manager & Director of Emergency Services
  Karl H. Berger, City Attorney

 SUBJECT:  Extending a Local Emergency for the Goodviews Abatement Project
  (“GAP”)

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Extend the local emergency for the GAP pursuant to Section 3 of Resolution No.
  2022-R101 (adopted December 21, 2022) to May 1, 2023; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

On December 21, 2022, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 2022-R101 that
extended the GAP local emergency until March 1, 2023. Since it adopted Resolution No.
2022-R101, the City experienced multiple rain storms in 2023 which led the City Council
to declare an additional local emergency to address the 2023 Winter Storms (Resolution
No. 2023-R5, adopted January 18, 2023). These ongoing Winter Storms are delaying the
completion date for the GAP. The engineer’s estimate for a completion date is now on or
about April 30, 2023.

BACKGROUND:

Pursuant to Resolution Nos. (collectively, the “Emergency Resolutions”) 12255 (adopted
June 16, 2021); 2022-R22 (adopted April 20, 2022); 2022-R34 (adopted May 18, 2022);
2022-R63 (adopted August 1, 2022); and 2022-R101 (adopted December 21, 2022) the
City Manager and City Attorney are exercising emergency powers to abate a public
nuisance in accordance with the Settlement Agreement in the civil case captioned The
People of the State of California, ex rel., Mark D. Hensley, City Attorney for the City of
Monterey Park v. Center Int’l Investments, Inc., et al. (filed December 31, 2015) LASC
Case No. BC605788. This is identified as the Goodviews Abatement Project (“GAP”). The
Emergency Resolutions allow the City Council to extend the local emergency by minute
order, i.e., without the need for a written resolution.

The 2023 Winter Storms (identified in Resolution No. 2023-R5) are interfering with
completion of the GAP. The contractor is currently scheduled to complete installation of
a retaining wall along West Garvey Avenue. Thereafter, it will be removing the impact wall
 Staff Report
Page 2 of 2

and installing the last row of tie back anchors into the bottom of the retaining wall. Next,
the retaining wall facing (i.e., the aesthetic “look”) will be placed. Concurrently (pending
the suspension of rain), final grading will commence to complete stabilization of the slope.

As part of the 2023 Winter Storm local emergency, the City installed temporary
winterization measures onto the property – but outside the GAP boundaries – to help
reduce the likelihood of additional sloughing.

FISCAL IMPACT:
There is no fiscal impact directly associated with the recommended action. All costs
associated with the GAP are well document including, without limitation, in the
abatement liens recorded against the real property.

Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD), and the Successor Agency (SA) of the

Wednesday, March 1, 2023 at 5:30 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER:
Mayor Sanchez called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL:
Mayor Sanchez called the roll:

Council Members Present:  Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Thomas Wong, Jose Sanchez,
  Yvonne Yiu

ALSO PRESENT: City Attorney Karl Berger, City Manager Ron Bow, Assistant City
Manager Inez Alvarez, Director of Finance Martha Garcia, and Deputy City Clerk Cindy
Trang. Representing Kidder Matthews, Negotiation Party for Item No. 2A, Bill Boyd
Executive Vice President and Linda Lee Executive Vice President

ORAL AND WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS: None.

1.  OPEN SESSION

1-A.  EXTENDING A LOCAL EMERGENCY FOR THE GOODVIEWS ABATEMENT
  PROJECT (“GAP”)

  On December 21, 2022, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 2022-R101 that
  extended the GAP local emergency until March 1, 2023. Since it adopted
  Resolution No. 2022-R101, the City experienced multiple rain storms in 2023
  which led the City Council to declare an additional local emergency to address
  the 2023 Winter Storms (Resolution No. 2023-R5, adopted January 18, 2023).
  These ongoing Winter Storms are delaying the completion date for the GAP. The
  engineer’s estimate for a completion date is now on or about April 30, 2023.
